tldr: Evening batch, Aug 17: OpenAI published 14 policy proposals for the Intelligence Age (funding independent projects on economic opportunity and resilience) as the US open-weight strategy gets a rethink — Bloomberg reports Nvidia and Meta's new open releases read as a tacit admission the moat isn't holding, with Qwen past 3B downloads in six months. Zhipu's GLM-5.3 claims the bug-finder crown over Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol on CyberGym, and Ling 3.0 (tiny 8B1B + flash 124B5B reasoning models) landed in llama.cpp. A DeepMind paper argues LLMs can't generate novel explanatory hypotheses, and The Decoder's critics question Anthropic's EU-AI-Act watermarking tradeoffs. Elsewhere: Microsoft's AI plans reportedly constrained by a chip shortage, Rakuten partners with Helsing on AI defense drones, Singapore hosts the world's first biological data center, and Hermes Agent keeps shipping — 19x faster desktop sessions and a 350K context window for Codex users — while DeepSeek's MIT-licensed Harness (already live) is the open rival to Claude Code.

articles.title: OpenAI's New Policy Ideas for the Intelligence Age
